subject: Intermittent 5xx & timeouts from Galeon7b — remediation timeline and customer playbook
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: infra-team@cloudcorp.com
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] Elevated 5xx/timeouts on Galeon7b (observed 08:45-09:05 PT)

Team —

We saw a concentrated window of elevated 5xx and request timeouts hitting Galeon7b in the us-west region between 08:45 and 09:05 PT. Error rates peaked at ~6.8% token-level 5xx and several long tail timeouts at the 10s+ latency range. Initial triage:

- Kernel-level memory pressure on a subset of worker VMs -> eviction/restarts observed in logs.
- KV cache thrashing correlated with sequences > 1.5k tokens.
- No config rollouts or customer-facing changes in the same window.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben: please loop in Aperture point of contact (Alyssa) and let them know we're investigating; recommend reducing max_seq if they can as a short mitigation.
2) Rafael: confirm whether autoscale responded and provide counts of restart events per host.
3) Hannah: can you coordinate a short bridge for customers and draft remediation guidance?

Attaching the initial metric window plus a short host-restart log excerpt.

Attachments: galeon7b-error-window-20260705.png, bridge-notes-20260705.docx

Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [Alert] Elevated 5xx/timeouts on Galeon7b (observed 08:45-09:05 PT)

Ben / Hannah —

Thanks for the heads up. We saw a spike in failed generations on our end starting ~08:50 PT; user-facing errors were primarily in the recommendation pipeline but also surfaced in our analytics cron. Impact estimate: ~3% of requests returned 5xx; some long-running requests retried once and succeeded, others failed end-to-end.

We've temporarily reduced our request concurrency and decreased max_tokens for long-history prompts. If you have a recommended playbook for this model (timeouts vs token length thresholds, retry backoff), we’ll follow it. Also: any ETA on stabilization?

—Alyssa
Director, Platform Engineering, Aperture Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@aperture-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 5xx & timeouts from Galeon7b — remediation timeline and customer playbook

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for confirming the impact and for the mitigation steps on your side. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood:

What happened (TL;DR):
- Between 08:45–09:05 PT Galeon7b in us-west experienced a short degradation window driven by worker-level memory pressure causing kernel restarts and KV cache thrash for long-context sequences. This produced elevated 5xx and some long tail timeouts for sequences > ~1200 tokens.

Customer-facing mitigations you can apply now:
- Reduce max_tokens to <= 1024 for critical endpoints (we recommend 512–1024 as safe).
- If you must keep long histories, use prefix caching where possible and avoid sending full chat history in every request.
- Use exponential retry with jitter: initial delay 250ms -> backoff x2 -> cap 3 retries. Avoid immediate tight retries.

Our actions and timeline:
- 10:00 PT: Throttled background maintenance jobs on the affected pool (completed).
- 10:25 PT: Deployed targeted kernel patch + host-level memory tuning to reduce OOM churn (Rafael).
- 10:40 PT: Autoscale policy adjusted to proactively spin additional warm workers for sequences > 1k tokens.
- 10:55 PT: Observed error rate fall back toward baseline (~0.4%).
- 11:05 PT: Full recovery confirmed in the primary host group; continuing to monitor for regressions.

Attachments: customer-playbook-galeon7b.pdf (concise playbook with recommended config), galeon7b-error-window-20260705.png

Short-term recommendations for Aperture:
1) Apply the token limit and retry guidance above for the next 24 hours while we monitor.
2) If you have queries that must use >1.2k tokens, mark them as non-critical or send with lower concurrency.
3) We'll send a brief post-incident note with root cause analysis and any downstream lasting mitigations by EOD.

I'll host a 30-minute bridge at 11:15 PT to walk through details and answer any questions. Tentative dial-in below. If that time doesn't work, let me know and Ben will coordinate.

Bridge: meet.redwood.com/bridge/galeon-20260705 (PIN: 6241)

Thanks —
Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Alyssa King <alyssa.king@aperture-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Galeon7b recovery confirmed + post-incident follow-up plan

Alyssa / Aperture team —

Follow-up from our 11:15 bridge: final status is stable; the primary issue was worker host churn due to an edge-case memory growth path triggered by long context sequences and a specific kernel allocation pattern. Important notes:

- What we fixed: targeted kernel tuning + host memory reservation improved stability; autoscaler warm pools now spin earlier for high-seq traffic profiles.
- What we're doing next (postmortem track):
  * Engineering (Rafael): full RCA and code-level remediation by 2026-07-12.
  * SRE (Priyom): host fleet health checks + alert tuning to catch this pattern earlier (ETA 2026-07-09).
  * Product (Hannah): model serving guidance doc (the attached playbook) will be updated and we'll notify customers with recommended safe defaults for Galeon7b by 2026-07-08.

We recommend Aperture keep the conservative request settings through 2026-07-09 while SRE finishes alert tuning. If any customer-critical requests require high-context length after that date, please open a priority support request and we'll coordinate dedicated warm capacity.

Closing notes: appreciate the quick collaboration — the customer bridge and your temporary throttles materially reduced end-user impact.

Attachments: bridge-notes-20260705.docx (internal bridge minutes), customer-playbook-galeon7b.pdf, galeon7b-error-window-20260705.png

Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
